title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test
title_zh: 评估基于空间的甲烷检测：一年期盲测评估
abstract: Space-based remote sensing allows detection and monitoring of large, concentrated methane sources worldwide1. However, independent evaluation of instruments and algorithms is limited, and new satellites and artificial intelligence techniques have not been tested under controlled, single-blind conditions2. Here we conduct a year-long, single-blind test involving 746 events: 481 methane releases of 9.5–1,183.7 kg h−1 and 265 blank controls. We released metered methane quantities in Arizona, USA, coinciding with overpasses from 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites. Fifteen analysis teams from nine countries generated more than 2,250 estimates, making this, to our knowledge, the largest controlled test so far and one of the first evaluations of the instruments EMIT, Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper) and GHOSt. Performance is heterogeneous: ‘built-for-purpose’ instruments designed to target methane demonstrate excellent detection performance (92–100% true positive rate, 0–11% false positive rate) and quantification accuracy (slope 0.83–1.00, 44% mean absolute percentage error). Instruments repurposed for methane sensing perform more variably (detection rates 62–88%, 46% mean absolute percentage error); still, many demonstrate significant skill. Broad land scanners detect poorly at tested rates but have consistent global coverage and historical archives, motivating additional work. Artificial intelligence-based methods show promise, but caution is warranted; 79% of false positives emerge from these methods. Ground-measured cloud cover >20% degraded performance across systems, raising concerns for use in some locations. Our findings show that satellite-based measurements can achieve accurate detection and quantification of methane point sources when the source location is approximately known. A year-long single-blind study shows that multiple satellites can accurately detect and quantify methane point-source emissions.
abstract_zh: 基于空间的遥感允许全球检测和监测大型、集中的甲烷源1。然而，仪器和算法的独立评估受到限制，新卫星和人工智能技术也未在受控的单盲条件下进行测试2。本研究进行了一年期的单盲测试，涉及746个事件：481次甲烷释放（排放量9.5–1,183.7 kg h−1）和265个空白对照。我们在亚利桑那州美国，在12颗政府、商业和非营利卫星的越轨期间释放了计量的甲烷量。来自九个国家的15个分析团队生成了2,250多个估计值，据我们所知，这是迄今为止规模最大的受控测试，也是对EMIT、Tanager-1（Carbon Mapper）和GHOSt仪器的首次评估之一。性能表现异质：‘专为特定目的’设计的仪器专门用于目标甲烷，表现出极佳的检测性能（92–100% 真阳性率，0–11% 假阳性率）和量化精度（斜率0.83–1.00，均方百分比误差44%）。专为其他用途改装的仪器在甲烷探测方面表现更加多样（检测率62–88%，均方百分比误差46%），尽管如此，许多仪器仍表现出显著的技能。广域土地扫描仪在测试的条件下检测性能较差，但具有全球一致的覆盖和历史档案，这激励了进一步的研究。基于人工智能的方法显示出希望，但需谨慎；79%的假阳性来自这些方法。测量的云覆盖>20%降低了各系统的性能，这引起了在某些地点使用的担忧。我们的研究表明，当源位置大约已知时，基于卫星的测量可以实现对甲烷点源的精确检测和量化。一年期的单盲研究表明，多颗卫星可以精确检测和量化甲烷点源排放。
